scope: Targeted primary-source update for the authorized part-3 smoothing-spline pilot. No algorithm edits, fitting or installation performed by this review.
recommended_hypothesis: Keeping the current Kennedy DR nuisance fits and exactly the same cross-fitted pseudo-outcomes xi, replacing only final Gaussian local-linear smoothing by cubic smoothing spline may reduce finite-sample level-curve error. This is an empirical task adaptation, not a new causal estimator or a complete Bonvini-Kennedy reproduction.

sources.title: Fast convergence rates for dose-response estimation
sources.publication: Author research page lists Electronic Journal of Statistics, to appear, 2026. No Fisher coauthor; not first proposed in 2026.
sources.evidence_location: Sections 2.1-2.2, Algorithm 1. In the HTML, lines 162-170 discuss independent samples and cross-fitting variants; lines 195-214 give ERM/linear-smoothing final regressions and explicitly list smoothing splines.
sources.supports: The continuous-treatment DR pseudo-outcome can be followed by a different regression/smoothing learner, including a smoothing spline. Global ERM and linear-smoother error analysis justify this as a principled candidate family.
sources.does_not_support: It does not establish that this candidate will improve the present sample, that the current clustered cross-fitting inherits all iid rates, or that level-curve improvement implies derivative/threshold improvement.
sources.replication_boundary: The paper analyzes a three-independent-sample construction, discusses alternative leave-one-out and multi-split constructions, and includes higher-order influence-function estimators. This pilot shares the existing Kennedy xi and changes only its last smoother. It does not reproduce the full BK estimator or experiments.
sources.author_code: No replication repository for this specific paper was located in targeted searches or its author research page. The GitHub Job Corps link in its application is a data source from Colangelo-Lee, not BK software. No unverified license assigned.
sources.why_not_higher_order_now: Higher-order correction requires projection-basis and Gram-matrix choices and extra estimation. The paper discusses singular Gram matrices and empirically used pseudoinverses. That is a separate multi-parameter research change rather than an isolated final-smoother comparison.

sources.official_api_checked: make_smoothing_spline(x,y,w=None,lam=None) returns a cubic BSpline. Its documented loss is sum_i w_i*(y_i-f(x_i))^2 + lam*integral(f''(u)^2 du). lam=None invokes ordinary GCV; an explicit nonnegative lam fixes the smoothing penalty. The documentation describes a clean-room implementation of the historical algorithm.
sources.license: BSD-3-Clause verified from the repository license text and repository license label. Reuse the maintained SciPy implementation rather than copying an unlicensed author package.
sources.maintenance: Current official API documentation and the active public SciPy repository were checked. The docs-linked source is version v1.18.0. This does not assert that v1.18.0 is installed locally or require upgrading the environment.
sources.conditions: Univariate amounts need ordered distinct abscissas for the smoother implementation and at least the API's required number of usable knots/points. If there are duplicate observed amounts, exact weighted collapse within the fitted training sample can preserve squared-loss contributions; do not remove observations or aggregate across validation boundaries.
sources.not_claimed: Ordinary observation-level GCV does not establish user-cluster-aware tuning or causal inference. No CPU runtime or new effect improvement measured by this literature task.

sources.title: Debiased inference for a covariate-adjusted regression function
sources.publication: JRSS Series B 87(1), February 2025, 33-55; DOI 10.1093/jrsssb/qkae041; online 2024-05-30. The primary arXiv version checked is v3 revised 2023-12-15, first posted 2022-10-12.
sources.purpose: Debiased local-linear point estimates, pointwise intervals and uniform bands without undersmoothing under its smoothness/nuisance/positivity assumptions.
sources.code: The author simulation repo describes exact numerical studies and depends on DebiasedDoseResponse. No explicit license located on the visible simulation-repository root. Package DESCRIPTION still contains the placeholder license-selection template. Do not call it MIT or copy its source under an assumed license.
sources.why_not_first: The immediate research question is whether final smoothing improves point-curve accuracy. TW changes bias correction and inference; it can increase variance. Reproducing its uncertainty procedure and adapting repeated-user inference would confound this small final-smoother experiment. Keep it for a dedicated later inference/threshold study.

sources.title: Debiased inference for proximal dose-response function
sources.evidence_location: Original PDF pages 6-8, section 2, Assumptions A and B; page 29 data availability.
required_data_and_assumptions: Observed baseline X plus a treatment-inducing confounding proxy Z and outcome-inducing proxy W.
Y conditionally independent of Z given U,X,A, and W conditionally independent of Z,A given U,X; exchangeability and positive treatment density conditional on U,X.
Completeness/injectivity conditions for proxy conditional-expectation operators.
Existence and square-integrability of outcome/treatment bridge functions satisfying its bridge equations.
sources.why_not_first: Existing ordinary factors have not been scientifically established as this pair of valid proxies. A newly generated hidden-confounding scenario alone does not supply such proxies or validate completeness. Simply renaming two existing factors as Z and W would not implement the identification assumptions.
sources.code_status: The paper's data availability points to https://github.com/yuchen-zhu/kernel_proxies for the earlier Mastouri et al. benchmark data. This is not evidence of a licensed implementation of this 2026 estimator. No new author implementation was established in the targeted title/code search.
sources.relevance: Useful future route only if actual proxy measurements and their scientific roles can be established. Its presence does not justify claiming that smoother replacement fixes unmeasured confounding.

formula_to_code_checks_C3.equation: SciPy: sum_i (xi_i-f(a_i))^2 + lambda_sum*integral(f''(a)^2 da). If the protocol uses mean_i squared error + lambda_mean*roughness, pass lambda_sum=n*lambda_mean for unit weights.
formula_to_code_checks_C3.reason: A fixed numeric summed-loss lambda implies a different relative penalty when sample size changes. Record which convention is used; for nonuniform weights explicitly fix their normalization.

formula_to_code_checks_C3.equation: For u=(a-a_min)/L and z=xi/T, f(a)=T*g(u), roughness in amount units equals T^2/L^3 times roughness in u. A summed-loss lambda_a becomes lambda_u=lambda_a/L^3 in the scaled objective; prediction derivative is (T/L)*g'(u).
formula_to_code_checks_C3.reason: Fix L and T before fitting so tuning and reported seconds/amount derivatives match the implemented objective. Outcome rescaling alone cancels from both quadratic terms; amount rescaling does not.

formula_to_code_checks_C3.equation: Candidate fit uses the exact same observed-dose xi values as the retained final smoother.
formula_to_code_checks_C3.reason: No new nuisance fits, GPS, hidden truncation, marginalization definition, reference dose, or weighting change inside the candidate. Any such change would alter the research question.

formula_to_code_checks_C3.equation: Estimated effect at a relative to a0 is f_hat(a)-f_hat(a0), compared with theta(a)-theta(a0).
formula_to_code_checks_C3.reason: Level-curve error and effect-contrast error differ because reference-dose error also enters. Predeclare the primary target and evaluate it identically.

formula_to_code_checks_C3.equation: Bounded observed Y does not imply xi is in [0,T].
formula_to_code_checks_C3.reason: Do not clip xi or final contrast to [0,T] merely to make the spline appear plausible; it changes the target/estimator. Preserve the baseline output contract.

formula_to_code_checks_C3.equation: Query the fitted BSpline at arbitrary a; derivative queries use the analytic spline derivative with the scaling chain rule.
formula_to_code_checks_C3.reason: No binned-dose regression or grid interpolation. Retain the same eligibility/support interval for both methods; global spline extrapolation does not establish unsupported causal effects.

statistical_design_issues: Use whole-user folds. Two events from one user are dependent; dense query points, paired scenarios and repeated events do not create independent sample-size blocks.

Cross-fitted pseudo-outcomes can share trained nuisance models across folds and are not iid independent regression responses in the exact theoretical sense. A paired empirical comparison is appropriate; do not claim the full BK iid guarantee for this implementation.

Freeze the lambda-selection policy on new development before accessing the fixed final truth/output. Ordinary GCV may be a baseline selector, but it must not be described as cluster-aware. A fixed development-selected lambda is clearer for this pilot.

If only the spline gets a new tuning search, any improvement is over the frozen current baseline, not a proof of superiority over every optimally tuned local-linear learner. State that comparison target correctly.
Curvature regularization can reduce variance and also flatten real saturation or nonmonotone structure. Report dose-wise errors and mechanism-specific results in addition to pooled RMSE.
Level or contrast RMSE improvement does not guarantee derivative RMSE, target crossing accuracy or subgroup support improves. These are independent downstream scores.

Global empirical risk is weighted by observed dose density, whereas a uniform query-grid RMSE weights the evaluation range differently. Selection loss and primary evaluation weighting must be declared; do not assume one guarantees the other.
User versus event target populations coincide in the present two-event-per-user design but may differ with uneven event counts later. Do not silently change target weights.
No confidence band based only on fixed cached nuisance fits should be described as complete causal uncertainty. This pilot can focus on point estimates without claiming new uncertainty coverage.

evidence_reporting_B6.performance_numbers: No new performance result in this review. All new gains must point to actual new development/final metrics and independent verification, not literature abstract rates.
evidence_reporting_B6.scientific_claim: The chosen smoother is a mature numerical/statistical method motivated by a recent continuous-DR framework. Its task-specific improvement, if any, must be established by this project's paired new-data experiment.
evidence_reporting_B6.source_rule_E: Technical claims above use the original articles, author repositories, and official SciPy documentation/license. Search aggregators were not used to establish method assumptions or reusable licenses.
